title: Summary Ranges
spaceBreakdown:
- int start: single variable → O(1)
- int i (loop counter): O(1)
- not counted: input vector nums, returned vector<string> result
approach: Since the array is already sorted and unique, consecutive integers form ranges. Scan left to right, tracking the start of the current range. When `nums[i]` is not exactly `nums[i-1] + 1`, the current range ends at `nums[i-1]`-emit it (as `"a->b"` or `"a"`), then begin a new range at `nums[i]`. After the loop, emit the final pending range. Using `long long` for the consecutiveness check avoids overflow when values span the full `int` range.
hints: The array is already sorted and unique. What relationship must two adjacent elements satisfy for them to belong to the same output range?
Linear scan tracking the start of the current range. For `nums = [0,1,2,4,5,7]`, start=0; at i=3, `nums[3]=4 ≠ 2+1`, so close range `[0,2]` and restart at 4.

```
start = nums[0]
for i = 1 to n-1:
    if nums[i] != nums[i-1] + 1:
        emit range [start, nums[i-1]]
        start = nums[i]
emit range [start, nums[n-1]]
```

**Empty input** - no elements to process
`Input: nums = []` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: accessing `nums[0]` without checking `n == 0` → undefined behavior / crash

**Single element** - loop body never executes, range must be emitted after the loop
`Input: nums = [7]` → `Expected: ["7"]`
⚠️ Bug: only emitting ranges inside the for loop, no post-loop emission → returns `[]`

**All separate** - every element is its own range, format must use `"a"` not `"a->a"`
`Input: nums = [0, 2, 4, 6]` → `Expected: ["0", "2", "4", "6"]`
⚠️ Bug: always using `"a->b"` format even when `a == b` → returns `["0->0", "2->2", "4->4", "6->6"]`

**Extreme values** - INT_MIN and INT_MAX in the same array
`Input: nums = [-2147483648, 2147483647]` → `Expected: ["-2147483648", "2147483647"]`
⚠️ Bug: using `nums[i] - nums[i-1] == 1` to check consecutiveness → signed integer overflow (UB) when computing `2147483647 - (-2147483648)`

followUps.q: What if the input array is not guaranteed to be sorted?
followUps.a: Sort it first, then run the same linear scan. Time complexity becomes O(n log n) due to the sort; space remains O(1) auxiliary (in-place sort).

followUps.q: What if the array may contain duplicates?
followUps.a: After sorting, skip duplicates by advancing `i` past consecutive equal values before checking consecutiveness. Time stays O(n log n); space stays O(1).

followUps.q: What if nums arrives as an unbounded stream and cannot fit in memory?
followUps.a: Keep only the previous value and the current range start in memory. On each new value, check consecutiveness against the previous; emit and reset when the streak breaks. Time is O(n) per element; space is O(1) (excluding output).
